cards.title: A leaving layer is a still, not a live scene: one live scene at any moment

cards.body:
## Summary
During every depth move the stage keeps the place you left as a fully live React scene until its leave animation ends, so two (up to three) scenes run their effects, listeners, fetches and frame loops at once. Make the leaving layer a static still captured at the move's start and unmount its live tree immediately, so exactly one scene is live at any moment by construction.

## Description
`layers.ts` already says what each layer is doing; `Stage.tsx` renders every layer through `SceneOf`, so a leaving layer is a live scene that is merely `inert`. The consequence is a rule every scene must remember: five scene files carry six hand-copied `closest('[inert]')` guards so a leaving copy does not answer a key, and ADR 0092's one-loop budget depends on the Voice studio remembering it. Effects without a guard (a poll, a subscription, a mic stop on unmount, a lightbox) still run twice for the length of the leave, and an interrupted move keeps up to three copies alive. The move: a pure `still.ts` that turns a layer's DOM into a static copy (deep clone, canvases copied by drawImage, ids and autofocus stripped, no listeners), a `live` flag on `Layer` (true only for the arriving or resting layer), and a `SceneLayer` that renders the still for a non-live layer instead of `SceneOf`. The snapshot is taken from the outgoing top layer's section at the moment the move is derived, before React commits the unmount. CSS keeps animating the section exactly as today (transform and opacity only, ADR 0089). The scene guards become dead code that a later pass in their own contexts may delete; this card does not touch them.

## Flow
- move derived in render (seq changed) -> snapshot the current top section into a still -> dispatch move -> React unmounts the left scene's tree (effects clean up now, not at animationend)
- leaving section shows the still and plays leave-*; arriving section mounts the one live scene
- animationend / SAFETY_MS flush removes the still; settle as today
- calm: no still, one layer at rest (unchanged)

## Expected impact
A whole class of defect closes: a leaving scene can no longer take a key, fire a fetch, keep a frame loop or a mic alive, or double a subscription during a move, for every scene present and future, with no guard to remember. Also halves React work during a move (one live tree instead of two or three). Technique: module-design locality-and-leverage (one rule at the stage instead of six copies in the scenes), motion performance-discipline (one loop, compositor-only leave).

## Evaluation
Claim: during and after a move exactly one scene is live, the leave still looks the same, and settle/flush/calm/chrome behaviour is unchanged.
Before: 3 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the three guards)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases, plus pnpm perf:stage for the clone cost at the move start
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.body:
## Summary
Rising from a depth today lands at the top of the place you came from with focus on the whole layer, so a person who dived into the fifth app, the third account or a Mind section scrolls and tabs back down every time. Make Rise and Escape keep the restore promise: the stage remembers each place's scroll and the element you left it from, and an up move restores both.

## Description
A pure `places.ts` holds a bounded, recency-ordered memory keyed by `formatHash(path)`: per place, the scrollTop of each scroller in the layer (by DOM order) and a locator for the element that had focus or was pressed when the move left (a data attribute or text-and-role locator, then a child-index path). The stage records the outgoing top layer at the move's start and, when an up move arrives at a recorded place, restores after the layer is drawn: scroll is applied when the content can hold it (a ResizeObserver retry with a short bound, abandoned on the person's own wheel, key or pointer scroll, so restored scroll never snaps back or fights the user), and focus goes to the remembered element, falling back to the layer. Down and across moves keep today's behaviour (a dive starts fresh). Page shape is untouched. Chores' topic keeps its own finer map; the two agree because both restore the same offset. Technique: session-resume layered-place-restoration (which layers restore, content-late snap-back, bounded records), app-shell lazy-section-loading warm return (returning lands where the user left), navigation-model (a move the user perceives as back returns them where they were).

## Flow
- dive from item-5 at scroll 400 -> places records #/apps {scroll:[400], focus:item-5}
- Escape / Rise / crumb (up move) -> arriving layer drawn -> scroll 400 applied when content is tall enough -> focus item-5
- dive again -> starts at top (unchanged)

## Expected impact
Every depth's way back becomes one press instead of rise-scroll-find-tab; a keyboard or screen-reader user returns to the row they acted on. The one hand-rolled copy (chores topic) is no longer the only place that keeps its place.

## Evaluation
Claim: an up move restores the left place's scroll and focus across all scenes, without changing dives, across moves or the page shape.
Before: 3 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the guards)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
